topic: Earthquake Focus, Epicenter, Magnitude and Intensity
key_concepts: Earthquakes are ground movements caused by sudden slip on a fault
The focus is the underground point where stressed rocks break and an earthquake begins
The epicenter is the point on Earth's surface directly above the focus
Fault lines and fault scarps are surface features associated with faulting
Seismographs record seismic waves produced by earthquakes
The triangulation method uses three seismic stations to locate an earthquake epicenter
Magnitude measures the energy released by an earthquake
Intensity measures how strongly an earthquake is felt at a given location
The Richter scale measures magnitude while the Mercalli scale measures intensity
PHIVOLCS uses an intensity scale to describe earthquake effects in the Philippines
Earthquake intensity generally decreases with distance from the epicenter
